papers.title: Experimental evaluation of post-processing techniques for fdm 3d-printed parts: solvent smoothing vs. laser smoothing, vibratory tumbling, and filler-primer coating
papers.abstract: Abstract This study directly compared four established surface-finishing methods for Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) parts: solvent-based chemical smoothing, CO₂ laser smoothing, vibratory tumbling, and filler-primer coating. The full comparison was performed on ABS and PLA specimens with surface inclinations of 10°–50°, while PVB-based PolySmooth and PolyCast were investigated only as supplementary reference materials for alcohol-based solvent smoothing and were excluded from the four-method comparison and ANOVA. Surface quality was evaluated using optical interferometry and ISO 25,178 areal surface-texture parameters. The as-printed S a ranges were 10.24–18.92 μm for ABS and 17.88–25.40 μm for PLA. Solvent smoothing provided the greatest roughness reduction on compatible polymers, reducing S a by 98.6–99.2% for ABS and 89.0–98.8% for PLA, while the supplementary PVB tests achieved average reductions of up to 99.56%. Surface conditions differed significantly at every investigated inclination for both S a and S t (Welch ANOVA, all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Pairwise Welch tests with Holm correction confirmed lower S a after chemical smoothing than after every other surface condition at all inclinations for both polymers. A comparative cumulative-cost model estimated average variable costs excluding labor and equipment investment of approximately 1.70, 0.64, 0.57, and 0.25 CZK per part for solvent smoothing, CO₂ laser smoothing, filler-primer coating, and vibratory tumbling, respectively, under the stated nominal batch assumptions. The results demonstrate that process selection requires balancing achievable surface quality against material compatibility, dimensional preservation, production volume, safety requirements, and economic constraints. The findings are limited to the investigated materials, specimen geometry, and selected post-processing conditions, without systematic process-parameter optimization or quantitative evaluation of dimensional and mechanical changes.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较FDM打印件多种表面后处理方法的减糙效果与成本。
summary_zh.method: 对ABS和PLA试样采用溶剂、CO₂激光、振动滚磨和填料底漆四种后处理，用光学干涉法测面粗糙度并做ANOVA。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to systematically compare established surface-finishing routes for FDM parts in terms of achievable surface quality and cost.
summary_en.method: ABS and PLA specimens at 10°–50° inclinations were treated by solvent smoothing, CO₂ laser smoothing, vibratory tumbling, and filler-primer coating, then characterized with optical interferometry and ISO 25178 areal parameters.
summary_en.result: Solvent smoothing yielded the largest roughness reduction (up to 99.2% in Sa for ABS) but at the highest variable cost, whereas vibratory tumbling was cheapest with the least improvement.
summary_en.validation: Surface quality was validated through optical interferometric measurements and Welch ANOVA with Holm-corrected pairwise comparisons.
